hook.en: You can easily say you prefer biryani to idli, but can you say it gives exactly 37 utils more? Ordinal utility only ranks.
hook.kn: ಇಡ್ಲಿಗಿಂತ ಬಿರಿಯಾನಿ ಇಷ್ಟ ಎಂದು ಸುಲಭವಾಗಿ ಹೇಳಬಹುದು; ಆದರೆ ನಿಖರವಾಗಿ 37 ಯುಟಿಲ್ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಬಹುದೇ? ಕ್ರಮಸೂಚಕ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತತೆ ಕೇವಲ ಶ್ರೇಣೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

objectives.en: Explain ordinal utility and monotonic preferences
Define indifference curve, indifference map and MRS
State the properties of indifference curves

narration.en: You can easily say you prefer biryani to idli, but can you say it gives exactly 37 utils more? Ordinal utility only ranks.
narration.kn: ಇಡ್ಲಿಗಿಂತ ಬಿರಿಯಾನಿ ಇಷ್ಟ ಎಂದು ಸುಲಭವಾಗಿ ಹೇಳಬಹುದು; ಆದರೆ ನಿಖರವಾಗಿ 37 ಯುಟಿಲ್ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಎಂದು ಹೇಳಬಹುದೇ? ಕ್ರಮಸೂಚಕ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತತೆ ಕೇವಲ ಶ್ರೇಣೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Ordinal utility analysis assumes the consumer can rank bundles but not measure satisfaction. Preferences are monotonic: a bundle with more of at least one good and no less of the other is preferred. An indifference curve joins all bundles that give the consumer the same satisfaction. A family of such curves is the indifference map; a curve further from the origin shows a higher level of satisfaction.

points.en: Indifference map: higher curve = higher utility

narration.en: An indifference curve joins bundles that give the same satisfaction. A set of these curves is the indifference map, and higher curves mean more satisfaction.
narration.kn: ಒಂದೇ ಮಟ್ಟದ ತೃಪ್ತಿ ನೀಡುವ ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಜೋಡಿಸುವ ರೇಖೆ ತಟಸ್ಥ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ. ಇಂತಹ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಗಳ ಗುಂಪು ತಟಸ್ಥ ನಕ್ಷೆ; ಮೇಲಿನ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ತೃಪ್ತಿ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Plot the bundles: 1 banana and 12 mangoes, 2 and 8, 3 and 5, 4 and 3. The consumer likes them all equally.
Between A and B he gives up 4 mangoes for 1 banana; then 3; then 2. This is the marginal rate of substitution.
Now an indifference map. Each curve further out gives more satisfaction, and the curves never cross.

narration.en: Plot the bundles: 1 banana and 12 mangoes, 2 and 8, 3 and 5, 4 and 3. The consumer likes them all equally.

caption.en: Every bundle on one curve gives the same satisfaction (here x₁ × x₂ is constant). Drag the bundle: curves further out are preferred, because more is better. The slope of the curve at the bundle is the MRS: how much of good 2 the consumer will give up for one more unit of good 1.
caption.kn: ಒಂದು ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಯ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಕಟ್ಟುಗಳು ಸಮಾನ ತೃಪ್ತಿ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಕಟ್ಟನ್ನು ಎಳೆಯಿರಿ: ಹೊರಗಿನ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಅಪೇಕ್ಷಿತ. ಬಿಂದುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಇಳಿಜಾರು MRS.

tryThis.en: Move the bundle along the blue curve from top-left to bottom-right. What happens to the MRS?
tryThis.kn: ಕಟ್ಟನ್ನು ನೀಲಿ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಯ ಮೇಲೆ ಮೇಲಿನ-ಎಡದಿಂದ ಕೆಳಗಿನ-ಬಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸರಿಸಿ. MRS ಏನಾಗುತ್ತದೆ?

tryThis.en: Find two different bundles that give exactly the same utility.
tryThis.kn: ಸಮಾನ ತುಷ್ಟಿಗುಣ ನೀಡುವ ಎರಡು ಬೇರೆ ಕಟ್ಟುಗಳನ್ನು ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಿರಿ.

tryThis.en: Why can two indifference curves never cross?
tryThis.kn: ಎರಡು ಉದಾಸೀನ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಗಳು ಏಕೆ ಎಂದಿಗೂ ಛೇದಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ?

title.en: Marginal rate of substitution and convexity

body.en: The marginal rate of substitution (MRS) is the amount of good 2 the consumer is willing to give up for one more unit of good 1 while staying equally satisfied. It is the absolute slope of the indifference curve. As the consumer has more of good 1 and less of good 2, he is willing to give up less of good 2 for each extra unit of good 1: MRS diminishes, which makes the indifference curve convex to the origin.

points.en: MRS = |Δx₂/Δx₁| = absolute slope of the IC
Diminishing MRS → IC convex to the origin

narration.en: The MRS is how much of good 2 the consumer gives up for one more unit of good 1. It falls along the curve, so the indifference curve is convex.
narration.kn: ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಘಟಕ ಸರಕು 1ಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಅನುಭೋಗಿ ಬಿಟ್ಟುಕೊಡುವ ಸರಕು 2ರ ಪ್ರಮಾಣವೇ ಸೀಮಾಂತ ಬದಲಿಕೆ ದರ. ಇದು ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುವುದರಿಂದ ತಟಸ್ಥ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ ಮೂಲಬಿಂದುವಿಗೆ ಪೀನವಾಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Indifference curves (1) slope downward from left to right, because with monotonic preferences more of one good must be balanced by less of the other; (2) are convex to the origin, because of diminishing MRS; (3) never intersect, because a common point would have to give two different satisfaction levels; (4) a higher curve shows a higher level of satisfaction.

narration.en: Indifference curves slope downward, are convex to the origin, never cross each other, and a higher curve means more satisfaction.
narration.kn: ತಟಸ್ಥ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಗಳು ಕೆಳಮುಖ ಇಳಿಜಾರು ಹೊಂದಿವೆ, ಮೂಲಬಿಂದುವಿಗೆ ಪೀನವಾಗಿವೆ, ಪರಸ್ಪರ ಛೇದಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಮತ್ತು ಮೇಲಿನ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ತೃಪ್ತಿ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

caption.en: An indifference curve x₂ = U/x₁. Change the satisfaction level U and slide along the curve to see the MRS fall.

Raise U. Where does the curve move?
Can two different U values give the same bundle? What does that say about crossing?

narration.en: An indifference curve x₂ = U/x₁. Change the satisfaction level U and slide along the curve to see the MRS fall.

problem.en: A consumer is indifferent between bundles A (1 banana, 12 mangoes), B (2, 8), C (3, 5) and D (4, 3). Find the MRS between successive bundles and comment on the shape of the curve.

steps.en: A → B: gives up 12 − 8 = 4 mangoes for 1 banana; MRS = 4.
MRS falls 4, 3, 2: diminishing MRS, so the indifference curve is convex to the origin.

answer.en: MRS = 4, 3, 2 (diminishing); the curve is downward sloping and convex to the origin.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A consumer is indifferent between bundles A (1 banana, 12 mangoes), B (2, 8), C (3, 5) and D (4, 3). Find the MRS between successive bundles and comment on the shape of the curve.

body.en: Slope Down, Higher is Happier, Never Cross, Convex. Say it as D-H-N-C.

narration.en: Recap. Ordinal utility ranks bundles; an IC joins bundles of equal satisfaction. MRS is the slope of the IC and it diminishes. ICs slope down, are convex, never intersect. A higher IC shows a higher satisfaction level.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಕ್ರಮಸೂಚಕ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತತೆ ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಶ್ರೇಣೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಸಮಾನ ತೃಪ್ತಿಯ ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಗಳನ್ನು ತಟಸ್ಥ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ ಜೋಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸೀಮಾಂತ ಬದಲಿಕೆ ದರ ತಟಸ್ಥ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಯ ಇಳಿಜಾರು; ಅದು ಕ್ಷೀಣಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ತಟಸ್ಥ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಗಳು ಕೆಳಮುಖ, ಪೀನ ಮತ್ತು ಛೇದಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಮೇಲಿನ ತಟಸ್ಥ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ತೃಪ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.
